# Registry of integrations without official public support

This file records only production features that depend on implementation details **not** covered by official public documentation or public schema, one table per product. The point is not to list everything that avoids the App Server, but to locate the real private dependencies quickly when a Desktop update breaks something.

**Verification baselines.** Codex Desktop `26.810.50856` (build `6644`) with built-in Codex CLI `0.148.0-alpha.9`, verified `2026-08-14`. The approval-routing and subagent rows were verified separately on Codex Desktop `26.818.41509` / CLI `0.149.0-alpha.4.1`, `2026-08-22`. Claude Desktop `1.30096.5` and Claude Code CLI `2.1.233`, verified `2026-08-16`; the Claude Code subagent row on CLI `2.1.241`, `2026-08-23`. Both tables' "a subagent stopped at a dialogue" rows were verified on Codex CLI `0.149.0-alpha.4.1` (isolated `CODEX_HOME`) and Claude Code CLI `2.1.241` (pty interactive session), both `2026-08-23`. The persistence timing behind "remove a Completed thread once read" was re-measured on Codex Desktop `26.820.60940`, `2026-08-26`. "Current progress on a Running row" was verified on built-in CLI `0.149.0-alpha.4.3`, `2026-08-25` — including comparing method visibility across the experimental and non-experimental schemas from `codex app-server generate-json-schema`, and polling a real in-flight Turn driven by a standalone `codex exec` once a second. "A stopped Codex Turn stops saying Running" was measured on CLI `0.151.0-alpha.7.1`, `2026-08-29`, by driving a real `codex app-server` in an isolated `CODEX_HOME` with all eight registrable hooks trusted and interrupting a live Turn. "A thread Codex will not hand over costs no read" was measured on Desktop `26.903.61454` / built-in CLI `0.153.4`, `2026-09-09`, by reading the twelve `*.command.input` hook schemas out of the shipped binary and comparing a live side chat's hook payloads with a persisted thread's.

"Officially publicly supported" covers the App Server, Codex Hooks, CLI/SDK interfaces and Desktop deep links defined in official documentation and public schema, plus the public macOS APIs used in the implementation. Merely not going through the App Server is not grounds for an entry. Official [Codex Hooks](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks) publishes the lifecycle events, the `hooks.json` location and the trust flow; official [Commands](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/reference/commands#deep-links) publishes the Desktop deep link. Neither is listed here.

**One observation deliberately not registered, recorded so nobody re-derives it.** Measured 2026-08-20: the trust key in `config.toml` has the shape `<hooks.json path>:<snake_case event>:<group index>:<handler index>`, where the third and fourth segments are array indices. That is a private detail, but **no feature reads it**: this app's two merge rules (append at the tail, write nothing when the install is already correct) are correct whether or not the observation holds — knowing it only explains why they carry the user's own definitions ([ADR 0014](adr/0014-the-codex-hook-definition-is-never-rewritten.md)). Per `AGENTS.md` §8.1 there is no row to add. Verifying trust no longer requires those private keys. Checked 2026-09-13: CLI `0.154.0-alpha.6.2` includes `hooks/list` and `HookMetadata.trustStatus` in its non-experimental public App Server schema. [CodexHookActivation.swift](../Notchline/Notchline/Products/Codex/CodexHookActivation.swift) uses that response and watches the documented configuration paths only as invalidation signals; it does not parse private keys or hashes. [CodexHookActivationTests.swift](../Notchline/NotchlineTests/CodexHookActivationTests.swift) covers matching and conservative fallback. This change adds, modifies, migrates and removes no non-public integration.

## Internal evidence boundary migration (2026-09-12)

[Generalisation package 1](product-generalisation-plan.md) moves the shared state machine to [MonitoringRepository.swift](../Notchline/Notchline/MonitoringRepository.swift) and [MonitoringState.swift](../Notchline/Notchline/MonitoringState.swift); the former `HookEventRepository` and state names remain compatibility aliases in [HookIntegration.swift](../Notchline/Notchline/HookIntegration.swift). Native decoding, projected requests, hook trust and held descriptors are owned by [HookEvidenceBoundary.swift](../Notchline/Notchline/HookEvidenceBoundary.swift). Rows below that name the old reducer refer to this same implementation through its alias. The private native fields, source discovery, write protocols and conservative degradation are unchanged; this is an internal boundary migration, not an added, removed or widened private integration. Existing native regression tests remain in their linked files; typed-source tests are in [MonitoringEvidenceConformanceTests.swift](../Notchline/NotchlineTests/MonitoringEvidenceConformanceTests.swift).

## Claude Code features

| Feature | What it is | Why the public interfaces cannot do it | How it is implemented | Dependency level and failure signals | Code |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Thread title | The expanded list shows each Claude Code thread under the title Claude Code itself uses, preferring a user-set title over a generated one. | The official hook payload gives `transcript_path` and no title; `claude agents --json` returns only a directory-derived `name`, which is the Project, not the title; no public interface reports a thread title. | Read-only on `~/.claude/projects/<dir>/<sessionId>.jsonl`, parsing `custom-title` and `ai-title` records and taking the last occurrence, user title first. The directory name is inferred by replacing every `/` in the working-directory path with `-`; **when that inference fails it falls back to searching the projects tree for `<sessionId>.jsonl` by filename**, so a change to the directory-naming rule alone cannot lose titles. Never a whole-file scan (a 16 MB transcript has been seen here): 64 KiB of the tail answers a session renamed while it runs, and the opening is read forward from the start in 64 KiB chunks until a title turns up, up to **128 records or 1 MiB, whichever comes first**. **That budget counts records because bytes were the wrong unit** — measured over the 480 titled transcripts here on 2026-09-11, the first title record is record 33 at the latest (p99 31) while its byte offset runs from 0 to 371 KB, because what stands in front of it is Claude Code's own opening and that is sized by the machine (the listings of skills, plugins, agents and MCP servers the session was started with), not by the session. A fixed 64 KiB head therefore stopped reaching it: on this machine that opening reached 87 KB with one 48 KB `skill_listing` record in it, and a live session drew `Untitled` with the name sitting in record 12 of its own transcript — 129 of those 480 are past the old window. The tail is cached on `(size, mtime)`; the opening is cached on its own, because a transcript is appended to and the bytes it read do not change — only a scan that ran out of *file* rather than of budget is redone, which is what lets a session named a moment after that read stop saying `Untitled`. Both are dropped when the session goes. A parse failure, an unrecognised record type or a missing file all return no title and the row shows `Untitled` — **never a fallback to the directory name**. With previews switched off it also shows `Untitled`, because a title is user content too. | **Claude Code private read-only schema.** Medium-high version risk. ## Antigravity features (CLI and Desktop)

Verified on Antigravity CLI `1.2.2` (`agy`, arm64), `2026-09-11`, in print mode and in a pty-driven interactive session, through a hooks file of this app's own; the transcript row was measured `2026-09-12` against the twelve conversations on this machine and one turn run for it, the read-state row the same day on a pty driving a whole turn of the real binary, and the live-line row the same day on two pty-driven TUI turns that recorded the transcript at every lifecycle event. Antigravity Desktop `2.13.0` was verified `2026-09-12` through the same registration, with turns driven in the running application ([`antigravity-desktop.md`](technical-explorations/multi-product-provider-architecture/antigravity-desktop.md)); the rows naming Desktop are that measurement. The product's hooks guide is embedded in both binaries and describes the events, the file and the payload's common fields; the rows below are what that guide does not promise. A Desktop row's click only raises the application, through public AppKit calls, and is not a row here.

The lock is held under an exclusive `flock` for exactly the process's life and the file is left behind unlocked, so the fd, not the file, is the evidence. | **Private layout.** A renamed directory or lock file makes every conversation read as closed the moment it starts: rows vanish seconds after their first event while `Connected` stays on. A renamed executable does the same. Signal: an Antigravity row that appears and is retired within one refresh while the CLI is visibly working. | `AntigravityConversationScanner` |
| The Turn boundary and its identity | One row per turn, opened at the turn's first model call and closed at its end, with the next turn of the same conversation replacing it. | The guide documents `invocationNum` and `executionNum` as fields and neither as a turn ordinal; measured, `executionNum` is 0 on every turn and no payload carries a turn id. | The translator opens a local Turn on `PreInvocation` with `invocationNum` 0, keeps later invocations of an open Turn out of the reducer (they feed only the live line, below), and closes it on `Stop`; a `Stop` with nothing open reuses the id it last retired. | **Measured behaviour of a documented field.** If a later build numbers invocations per conversation rather than per turn, every turn after the first never opens: the row of the first turn stays Completed while the CLI works. Signal: rows titled `Untitled` while the CLI plainly shows the prompt; `AntigravityTranscriptFileTests` fails. ## Capabilities deliberately not in this table

- The live Turn lifecycle bridge and hook install / upgrade / master switch / removal use official Codex Hooks, public events and the `hooks.json` configuration location.
- Claude Code session **discovery** uses the official public `claude agents --json` — its `--help` explicitly promises that `--json` prints active sessions including interactive ones and needs no TTY. The `status` / `waitingFor` fields in the same output are a different matter: the command is public, while those fields' existence, vocabulary and semantics are not, and they decide business state, so they are **registered separately above**.
- Claude Code's hook events, the `type: "command"` handler (including the `args` exec form and `timeout`) and the `hooks` configuration location in `~/.claude/settings.json` are all official public capabilities. This app **does write** that file's `hooks` key ([ADR 0016](adr/0016-write-the-users-claude-code-settings-and-keep-a-copy.md), superseding the earlier never-write [ADR 0010](adr/0010-never-write-the-users-claude-code-settings.md)), copying the original to `settings.json.notchline-backup` in the same directory first (and likewise `hooks.json.notchline-backup` for `~/.codex/hooks.json`). It writes an officially public configuration location in an officially public handler shape, so this is still not a private dependency. The helper that handler points at and the Unix domain socket it connects to are both inside this app's own support directory, and `/usr/bin/nc` ships with macOS; none of the three is a private dependency. The previous `type: "http"` was equally public, and the reasons for replacing it have nothing to do with publicness ([ADR 0013](adr/0013-claude-code-hooks-run-a-helper-not-a-port.md)).
- **A Claude Code row's content preview is also not registered**, even though the same row's **title** is. Their sources differ: a title can only be had by parsing a private transcript JSONL, while the preview comes from the official `MessageDisplay` hook — officially described as "While assistant message text is displayed", with the official payload `turn_id, message_id, index, final, delta`, over the `type: "command"` handler already in use. Neither a private schema nor a private path, so per [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md) §8.1 it is not an entry.
- **The process-ancestor-chain calls used for navigation** (`sysctl(KERN_PROC_PID)`'s `e_ppid`, `proc_pidpath`) and **the Apple Events used to focus a terminal tab** are not grounds for an entry: the former are public APIs, and the latter go through Terminal.app's and iTerm2's **own public scripting dictionaries**, unrelated to Claude Code. What is registered above is **the process shape "an ancestor is `Claude.app` means desktop-hosted" and that bundle identifier**.
- **The three BSD calls used for terminal read state** (`sysctl(KERN_PROC_PID)`, `devname_r`, `stat`) are public APIs, of the same nature as `NSWorkspace`'s activation notification, and are not themselves grounds for an entry; what is registered above is **the observed CLI behaviour of focus reporting**, because that path's coverage depends on it.
- Opening a Desktop thread exactly uses the official `codex://threads/<thread-id>` deep link and public macOS Launch Services.
- Quota, today's tokens, thread lists, titles, Turn detail and status correction use public App Server methods.

## Triage order after a Desktop update

1. Record the new Desktop short version, build and built-in `codex --version`. Advance this file's verification baseline only after re-verifying the private dependencies in the tables.
2. Run `NotchlineTests` first and use the failing tests to locate the feature.
3. Inspect private dependencies read-only: confirm the file, identifier or executable path still exists, then confirm the minimum schema. Never modify `app.asar`, inject into Desktop IPC, or dress a missing value up as success.
4. If official documentation or public schema has gained an equivalent capability, migrate to it and remove the corresponding private implementation notes from these tables.
5. If a feature is temporarily broken it must fail closed: `Project unavailable` for Project; thread status holds its last trustworthy value among the four, with global Disconnected only for an unresponsive App Server; never fall back to guessing from cwd, titles, timing or window focus.

## Maintenance rules

- Any new production feature depending on undocumented or uncommitted Codex implementation details must add or update a row here in the same change.
- Never register something merely because it avoids the App Server: official Hooks, official deep links, public CLI/SDK interfaces and public macOS APIs are all permitted implementations.
- Every row keeps at least the feature definition, the capability gap in the officially supported interfaces, the real implementation, the failure signals, and the code locations.
- A private schema must have fixture tests, missing/corrupt tests and an explicit conservative degradation; a parse failure must never be interpreted as an empty set or as `Chats`.


### Generalisation package 5 boundary update

[CodexRolloutTurnEvidence.swift](../Notchline/Notchline/Products/Codex/CodexRolloutTurnEvidence.swift) now returns phased values from [SupplementaryMonitoringEvidence.swift](../Notchline/Notchline/SupplementaryMonitoringEvidence.swift), applied by the shared repository. The Provider still supplies the same App Server rollout paths; identity confirmation still precedes abort reading. The Provider's explicit shutdown now also stops its existing Hooks/rollout sources, invalidates observation and parks deadlines; internal App Server reconnects keep their current recovery. This narrows internal authority and changes no private schema, source discovery, native write operation or conservative degradation. Existing native regression fixtures remain in [NotchlineTests.swift](../Notchline/NotchlineTests/NotchlineTests.swift); generic composition checks are in [MonitoringSourceCompositionTests.swift](../Notchline/NotchlineTests/MonitoringSourceCompositionTests.swift). No private feature was added, removed or widened.

Exact navigation raises the owning renderer window with the native host’s `focusWindow` in Force mode, asking again until focus lands or 1.5 seconds pass, and requires `document.hasFocus()` together with the selected native ID. If either cannot be confirmed, Notchline reports only an application raise. A refused navigation leaves observation running. `window.focus()`, used before companion 1.2.2, is ignored without a user gesture and left the last focused window in front; the measurements are in [the Trae integration](trae-integration.md).

## Connection discovery and presentation amendment

The connection refactor **modifies existing private dependencies**; it does not add a private Codex trust-state reader. The public macOS APIs provide application enumeration and Launch Services lookup, but the product bundle identifiers remain observed identifiers rather than a documented Codex compatibility promise. `ProductInstallationDiscovery` in [ProductConnection.swift](../Notchline/Notchline/ProductConnection.swift) reuses the existing Codex identity for bounded installation discovery. A changed identifier produces `App not found` or an unverified check, never an inferred connection. It checks running instances before conventional locations. [ProductConnectionTests.swift](../Notchline/NotchlineTests/ProductConnectionTests.swift) pins absence, uncertainty, presence and recovery separation.

Trae retains the existing private default-profile `extensions.json` dependency and now verifies the named extension's actual `package.json` identity/version. Missing files differ from unreadable or structurally incompatible files; the latter fail closed and offer rechecking, not coercion. Application discovery can select a non-default location; multiple unresolved installations refuse setup. These remain installation-layout and native identity dependencies. [TraeInstallation.swift](../Notchline/Notchline/Products/Trae/TraeInstallation.swift), [TraeProvider.swift](../Notchline/Notchline/Products/Trae/TraeProvider.swift), [TraeConformanceTests.swift](../Notchline/NotchlineTests/TraeConformanceTests.swift) and [the connection contract](product-connections.md) document the exact boundary. A product update breaking the manifest/package shape produces `Unable to check setup` or `Setup needs repair`; an unknown profile or window is not invented as a confirmed failure.
